facts.text: King Tuscar is a level-85 hrimthursa with 300,000 health, fought beside Queen Kula as the glacier's final.
He boasts that Kula wields the finest weapon he ever made, and that his own is almost as good.
At half health he 'gains strength from Odin', hits harder and starts Mjolnir's Fury and Thor's Might blasts around him and a bleed.
When Kula dies first he screams in rage and gathers more strength.
Allakhazam lists him at level 85; he drops Tuscar's swords, axes, hammers, bows and runic shields. A 2003 visitor said he looked like an ordinary hrimthursa, not a king.
The glacier is named for him, but bot chat already notes that only Kula is talked about.

story:
Tuscar was a smith before he was a king, and in his heart he is a smith still. The rime giants say he learned his craft at a forge so old that the first spearheads of the gods were quenched in its trough, in the days when giants and gods still traded, before the wall around Asgard was built and paid for with a trick. He took away more than the trade. He took an oath-word of Odin's, they say, burned into the haft of his hammer while the god's back was turned, and he has carried it ever since. Nobody knows if that is true. What is known is that he calls on Odin when he bleeds, of all the names a giant might call, and something answers.

Every weapon of Tuscaran is his work: the axes of the bladehands, the crushers of the icelords, the hammers of the throne guard. When he heard that the coldest daughter of Bergelmir had raised a citadel on a dragon's bones, he made the finest axe of his life and carried it across the island to her. She took it. Then she took him, and gave him a throne beside hers and a crown he was told to wear at feasts. He minds less than the skalds think. He has his forge in the back of the throne hall, and he has a queen who carries his best work into every fight, and he tells anyone who reaches the thrones that his own weapon is almost as good.

In a fight he is all forge-heat in a cold hall. His blows open wounds that keep bleeding, the scar of the gods, he calls it. Cut him to half and the old oath answers: he roars Odin's name, his strength rises, and the blows come down around him as Mjolnir's Fury and Thor's Might, hammer-strokes and thunder on everyone close enough to be hit by a smith. Kill Kula before him and he forgets the forge entirely. He screams for her, and gathers his strength, and fights like a widower who has nothing left to make.

The iarn dwarves, who know something about smiths, say the saddest thing in the glacier is not the frozen army or the last cell. It is the forge behind the thrones, where the fire is kept lit every day for a king who is only ever asked to make weapons.
legend: Raid leaders call him the anvil: he looks like any other hrimthursa until you are standing in front of him. A visitor in 2003 said he didn't look like a king at all, just a big giant, and then found out. Tanks rotate on him because his bleed stacks up. When he hits half, the hammer and thunder blasts land around him on everyone close, so melee step out for a beat, then back in. Some say kill him first so Kula's rage comes later; some say kill Kula first so his bleeds stop sooner. Nobody says split them. His weapons drop for every class and every guild wants one.

loremasterTopic.text: A smith first and a king second. He forged Kula's axe and boasts of it still. The rime giants say an oath-word of Odin's is burned into his hammer, and that it answers him when he bleeds. Whether that is true, he calls the All-Father's name at half his strength, and the hammers come down.

bookPage: From the workbook of Hroald, weaponsmith of Bjarkan. I was shown, by a Valkyn who had been inside, a broken axe-head of hrimthursa make. It was ice and it was steel, both at once, and the edge would not dull on my stone. I have made weapons for forty years and I do not know how it was done. The Valkyn said the king of the glacier made it, and that he makes them all, and that he is happiest at his forge and least happy on his throne. I believe it. A smith who could make that edge would not want to be bothered with anything as dull as a crown.
